title: State Bicycle Co 6061 All-Road v2
content:
Today, State Bicycle Co. launches the 6061 All-Road v2, its fastest and best-equipped gravel bike under $1,500…

The 6061 All-Road comes in three colorways at $1,499.99, two wheel sizes, and four frame sizes. Against v1, it is a generational change, not a refresh: new frame, new standards, new drivetrain, new brakes, new wheels. One fast drop-bar bike for mixed surfaces — pavement, fire road, gravel events — at a price where you normally cannot get modern frame standards. There are three colors: Liquid Emerald (green), Chrome Red, Metallic Smoke (graphite), four izes: X-Small 48cm, Small 51cm, Medium 54cm, Large 58cm, with two wheel options: 700c or 650b, same frame, same clearance, chosen at checkout.

6061 All-Road V2 Quick Hits:

  • Aero tubing. Double-butted 6061 shaped from the same aero profiles as our best-selling 6061 track frames. Profiled tubes plus fully hidden cables cut the drag a round-tube gravel frame gives away. The painted “anodized” finish is part of it — the aluminum shows through rather than sitting under paint.
  • Fully internal routing. An ID52 head tube takes the hoses from the bar through the headset and down the steerer. v1 ran a cable cradle on the outside of the fork.
  • T47 and UDH. T47 is threaded, so it cannot creak like a press-fit, and any shop can service it with normal tools. UDH is the bigger one: a SRAM Transmission derailleur bolts straight to the frame with no hanger. That upgrade path is rare under $1,500.
  • Tire clearance. The stock Continental is spec’d as a 29 x 2.0 — a two-inch tire on a gravel bike. Maximum clearance is 700c x 55mm or 650b x 55mm.
  • Wheels. 25mm internal width is the number to lead with: it is what lets a 50mm tire sit square instead of bulging. Add 30mm depth, 32 spokes, brass nipples. Tubeless ready out of the box — taped and valved, just add sealant.
  • Aero crankset. Solid narrow-wide 42T, 7075 ring on forged 6061 arms, 29mm spindle. The 49.7mm chainline sits outboard of a road crank, which helps the frame clear a 2.0in tire.
  • 12-speed, 11–46t. Range widens to 418%, with a low gear of 0.91:1, and because the 50mm tire is taller, the top end gains about 3% as well. Both ends open up. The derailleur is rated to 50T, so there is headroom for a mullet setup later.
  • Trail saddle. 150mm wide, for longer days on the bike.
  • Carbon levers, full hydraulic. A sealed hydraulic line from lever to caliper, so power and modulation hold up in the wet and at the bottom of a long descent. 160mm rotors front and rear.

Why it rides the way it does: 445mm chainstays and 73mm of BB drop make it planted at speed and on loose descents. A 50mm fork offset with a taller tire puts trail at roughly 73–78mm on the small sizes and about 68mm on Medium and Large — calmer without going vague. Head angles are size-specific: 70° on XS and S, 71.5° on M and L; most brands at this price run one angle across the range and let small riders deal with it.

Check out more info on the 6061 All-Road v2 at State Bicycle Co.
